description: Record a talk, type notes, get a transcript. All on your own machine. No account, no cloud, no network.

summary.one_liner: Blab is an offline, local-first desktop app that records a talk, takes typed notes alongside it, and transcribes the recording on your own machine using bundled Whisper speech models.
summary.what_it_does: Blab records audio while you type notes, then runs Whisper speech-to-text locally when you press Stop, producing a transcript next to your notes. Clicking a transcript line plays the audio from that moment. Each recording is saved as three plain files in a user-chosen folder: audio.webm, notes.md and transcript.md, with no database. It offers live captions during recording, a Windows-only option to record system audio for meetings, import of existing audio files, and export of .srt and .vtt subtitles or a plain text block. The app picks a speech model suited to the machine (Best, Balanced or Fast), and the installers bundle all three models so no later download is needed. The README states the app is designed to block all outgoing network connections.
use_cases: transcribe a recorded lecture or talk offline
take notes while recording a presentation
convert an audio file to subtitles (srt/vtt)
how_to_run: Download the installer for your OS from the releases page (Blab-Setup-*.exe, Blab-*.dmg, or Blab-*.AppImage)
Windows: run the installer and choose Run anyway on the SmartScreen prompt
Mac: drag Blab into Applications and approve it in System Settings > Privacy & Security
Build from source: git clone the repo, cd Blab, npm install, npm run setup (downloads models, needs internet), npm run app
Package an installer for your OS with npm run package
notable: Runs Whisper speech-to-text fully offline; installers bundle all three models (about 758 MB download)
Notes typed during recording are aligned with the transcript; clicking a line plays audio from that point
Each recording is three plain files (audio.webm, notes.md, transcript.md) with no database
Silero voice-activity detection removes silence before transcription, and timestamps map back to the original recording
Detects repetitive transcription loops and reports them to the user
caveats: Installers are unsigned, so Windows and macOS show security warnings on first run
System audio recording is Windows only
The window must stay open during transcription; closing it stops the job
Linux AppImage may need libfuse2 on Ubuntu 22 and older, and requires the --no-sandbox flag
